title: Perf run 20261020-0715
heading: No speed change held; the frame pacer gets a cap, two checks now fail on broken code, and two copies of engine code are gone
meta: This general run kept four changes: a cap on the frame pacer's pass loop, a stronger damage check, one shared copy of the pawn capture table and of the key generator, and a benchmark row for the lobby's scene. None of them claims a speed win, and the final A/B calls no primary row better or worse. The branch is improve/20261020-0715 from base bd26e1c; main did not move during the run. Every figure is from software rendering (SwiftShader) on a 4-vCPU VM, and each names the commits it compares.

needs.intro: Nothing here blocks the merge. All four items are information.

items.title: Information: two primary rows lean slower in the final A/B, neither called
items.body:
On f163681 against bd26e1c, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-0715-final.md):

  • Reopening a long game: 123 → 133 ms, median pair ×1.140, 6 of 10 pairs worse. The pairs run from 0.57 to 1.69.
  • The player's move appears: 151 → 161 ms, median pair ×1.102, 6 of 10 pairs worse. The pairs run from 0.74 to 1.32.

The code these rows run is the same on both sides. The pawn table and the key generator moved file without a change of text. The pass cap stops the loop only when a render returns before it reaches the backdrop's hook. In the app that happens only while the WebGL context is lost, which none of the benchmark's runs do, so their frames draw the same passes on both sides; damage.spec reads the board's own frames and finds them identical to whole ones. The same rows went the other way in this run's other A/Bs of nearly the same code: the player's move was ×0.929 in ab-20261020-0715-mw1b.md, and reopening leaned ×1.167 at step 2 on the base itself.
items.recommend: No decision needed. Read reopening and the player's move again in the next run's step 2, with 10 or more pairs.

items.title: Information: the 1.2× target is not met on any row
items.body: This run kept no speed change. Its one speed attempt, MW1 (the later passes of a frame keep the first pass's matrices), cut the CPU time to prepare a move's picture by about 25%, but neither of its two A/Bs called it, and no primary row moved. The run's other time went to checks and fixes that the review asked for.
items.recommend: No decision needed. The speed leads are at the top of the ledger for the next speed run.

items.title: Information: five rows leaned slower on the base itself at step 2, none called; three traced to the last run's PR
items.body:
On bd26e1c against 2f25230, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-0715-regress.md):

  • The start page usable, desktop: 65.6 → 68.1 ms, median pair ×1.033, 7 of 10 pairs worse. The pairs run from 0.95 to 1.18.
  • The start page answers its first click, desktop: 10.7 → 13.7 ms, median pair ×1.268, 9 of 10 pairs worse. The pairs run from 0.93 to 1.71.
  • A shared game's page, first screen: 92.8 → 100 ms, median pair ×1.034, 5 of 10 pairs worse. The pairs run from 0.90 to 1.47.
  • Reopening a long game: median pair ×1.167, 5 of 10 pairs worse. The pairs run from 0.60 to 1.63. Its diagnostic "replaying and showing the record" went 53 → 80 ms, 8 of 10 pairs worse.
  • A finished game's review: 2.04 → 2.12 s, median pair ×1.056, 6 of 10 pairs worse. The pairs run from 0.92 to 1.10.

A split (ab-20261020-0715-bisect-owner.md: main before #201 against 2f25230, 8 pairs) shows that the owner's PRs #192–#200 move none of the first click, reopening and the review: first click ×1.029, reopening ×0.940, review ×0.981. So those three come from #201. The other two are small and did not hold: the start page on desktop was ×1.003 in the split and ×1.024 in the final A/B, and the shared game's first screen (not measured in the split) was ×1.000 in the final A/B. The first click's share is RT1 (×1.103 alone at 10 pairs, ab-20261020-0008-rt1-coldload.md): since RT1 the lobby's canvas mounts in the same commit as the side choice. Reopening's replay leaned ×1.26 on #201 alone in the last run's final A/B, likely the same mechanism (the game's canvas now commits with the move record). #201 was not bisected further.

LC1, the fix aimed at the first click's lean (mount the lobby's canvas a frame after the side choice), was not built: under full motion the side choice's words wait for the lobby scene's first frame, so the row times a page commit that the player does not see, and a later mount would move that time stamp, not the picture. This run added a row that times the scene itself (see Changed).
items.recommend: No decision needed. LC1 stays open in the ledger, to be judged against the new scene row; reopening is read again at the next step 2.

items.title: Information: the lobby scene comes close to its 1.5 s fallback on a phone's first visit
items.body: On a phone's first visit (4× CPU, Fast 4G), the lobby's scene draws 1.51 s after the first click on f163681 and 1.52 s on bd26e1c, at the median. The lobby has a fallback that starts the page's entrance 1.5 s after it mounts if the scene has not drawn. In the final A/B no load reached the fallback (0 of 100 phone loads), but the margin is about 100 ms.
items.recommend: No decision needed. Ledger 0715:LL1 holds it: if loads start to reach the fallback, preload the lobby's chunk in the start page's idle time.

scoreboard.intro: The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. Each bar is a row's median pair, head divided by base; below 1 means faster. The dashed line is the target, 1.2× faster than the base.

items.title: Final A/B: the branch against the base, all 16 primary rows
items.body: f163681 against bd26e1c, 10 pairs, 73 minutes (ab-20261020-0715-final.md): ×0.991 over 16 rows, none called. All 117 diagnostics are unchanged within their noise. Memory is flat: JavaScript memory after reopening is −0.2%, and geometries and textures grow the same over 16 plies on both sides. The start page downloads 0.5 KiB less on desktop and 0.4 KiB less on the phone. Search speed is ×1.013, not called.

items.title: Step 2: the base against the last run's base
items.body: bd26e1c against 2f25230, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-0715-regress.md). The last run's changes hold: joining's first board picture is ×0.811 and the computer's ×0.774, and the player's move is ×0.688 and the opponent's ×0.689. All four are called better, and no row is called worse. Three rows lean slower without being called: the desktop first click ×1.268 (9 of 10 pairs worse), reopening ×1.167 (its replay 53 → 80 ms, 8 of 10 worse) and the review ×1.056; all three trace to #201 (see Needs from me). One diagnostic is called worse: the CPU time to prepare the player's move's picture, 1.63 → 2.85 ms. That is the cost of the last run's extra passes, and MW1 below tried to take it back.

changed.intro: Each change is its own commit. Its evidence is listed with it.

items.title: The frame pacer draws at most MAX_PASSES passes a frame (e06673c, ledger 0008:PL2)
items.body:
The pacer's pass loop ended only when a render reached the backdrop's onBeforeRender hook. A render that returned early made the loop run without end and froze the page. In the app that happens only while the WebGL context is lost, when three.js returns from every render at once; the benchmark's runs never lose it. The loop now stops at MAX_PASSES, the most passes that passes() can return, so a normal frame draws exactly what it did before.

Evidence: the new case in framePacer.test.tsx fails on the base (100 renders for a nextPass that stays true, against 4) and passes on the branch. One gap is left: after such a frame, the backdrop keeps a stale pass for the next frame (ledger 0715:PX1).

items.title: damage.spec reads the board's own frames; damage.test pins two more rules (0d22817)
items.body:
damage.spec drew its own partial frames, so it could not see a pacer that left a pass undrawn. It now reads each frame back as the pacer left it, draws the same frame whole, and compares the two pixel for pixel. It also requires that some compared frames took more than one pass. damage.test now checks that a mark's own damage box (damageBox) bounds its rect, and that the pass cost decides between one union rect and two rects.

Evidence: each check was made to fail on a broken copy of the code. With the pacer cut to one pass, 17 frames differ; with matrices left stale in part, 33 differ (the old spec passed this one). damage.test fails when screenRect ignores damageBox, and when PASS_COST is 0. All pass on the branch.

items.title: A benchmark row for the lobby's scene (effd21f, corrected in f163681)
items.body:
Under full motion, the side choice's words wait for the lobby's scene to draw its first frame. The old first-click row timed a page commit that the player does not see. The new cold-load row, "first click: the lobby's scene drawing", times the click to that first frame. The review found that it also counted the lobby's 1.5 s fallback timer as a frame; it now counts only the scene's own frame and counts the loads that reach the fallback in a row of their own.

Final A/B, base side: desktop 512 ms, phone 1.52 s, phone returning 915 ms. No load reached the fallback.

items.title: The scoreboard tool keeps the primary rows (f163681)
items.body: tools/ab2jsonl.mjs --only dropped the primary rows that its header said it kept, so this run's scoreboard had no primary rows for MW1. Evidence: with --only '^nomatch$' on ab-20261020-0715-mw1.md, the base's tool appends 0 rows and the branch's appends 5, all primary. The MW1 and LM1 rows were appended again in full.

removed.intro: Product code: net −9 lines (engine +18/−15, ai +12/−25, three +3/−2). Tests grew by 63 lines and the benchmark by 23.

items.title: One pawn capture table and one splitmix32 for the engine and the computer (ababfbb)
items.body: The pawn's five capture directions were written out three times (engine/board.ts, ai/position.ts, ai/kpk.ts) and the key generator splitmix32 twice (engine/draws.ts, ai/position.ts). Each now has one copy, in engine/pieces.ts and engine/draws.ts, with the same order and the same seeds. Evidence: the engine's tests pass, position.test checks every move list of the computer's board against the engine, and kpk.test passes. The search speed row is flat (×1.013, not called).

rejected.intro: Each result names its A/B report or patch in bench/loop/.

items.title: MW1: a frame's later passes keep the first pass's matrices
items.body: Against bd26e1c, 8 pairs (ab-20261020-0715-mw1.md): the time to prepare the player's move's picture went 2.83 → 2.02 ms, 7 of 8 pairs better, but the player's move leaned worse, ×1.097 (6 of 8). Again with 10 pairs (-mw1b.md): 2.60 → 1.95 ms, 10 of 10 better, not called because the pairs spread by more than the change; the player's move was ×0.929. Reverted; the patch is patches/0715-MW1-matrix-skip.patch.

items.title: LM1: one canvas measure setting for the game's and the lobby's canvases (parked)
items.body: Against ababfbb, 6 pairs (ab-20261020-0715-lm1.md): the desktop lobby scene came 514 → 476 ms sooner, called better, but joining's first board picture leaned worse, 861 → 891 ms (×1.033, 5 of 6). Parked as patches/0715-LM1-canvas-measure.patch until a 10-pair A/B of joining.

items.title: PS2 and BF1: cheaper pass planning and one bench fence per frame (parked)
items.body: A probe with temporary marks on 1,575 move frames found at most 42 parts a frame, passes() at most 0.2 ms, and the bench's fence at most 0.1 ms a pass: too little to win on move frames. The probe was not saved and did not count the frames PS2 names (the glaze switch, a review jump, the game's end), so both rows stay open, waiting on TR1's count.

items.title: LC1: mount the lobby's canvas after the page's commit (not built)
items.body: LC1 aimed at the desktop first click's lean since RT1 (10.7 → 13.7 ms at step 2, ×1.268, 9 of 10 pairs worse, not called). But under full motion the side choice's words wait for the lobby scene's first frame, so that row times a page commit that the player does not see. A later mount would move that time stamp, not the picture. The ledger now says to judge LC1 against the new scene row.

items.title: MW1 reverted although 17 of 18 pairs were better
items.body: It is a diagnostic that improved, not a moment a player waits on, and neither A/B called it. The patch is kept for a retry together with another per-pass cut.

items.title: The final leans are reported as information, not as a trade-off
items.body: The code on the paths of reopening and the player's move is the same on both sides, and the same rows leaned the other way in other A/Bs of this run.

items.title: No engine-tier A/B for the removal
items.body: The moved functions keep their text, and the primary search row is flat. The engine's move-list fixtures and board.reference.test pass.

items.title: The lost-context stale pass (PX1) is logged, not fixed
items.body: Before the cap, the same case froze the page; after it, one frame may draw a stale rect until the next redraw. A fix needs a unit test of the backdrop's lost-context path, which the run did not have time for.

items.title: The probe figures behind PS2 and BF1
items.body: They come from temporary marks that were not saved, so nobody can run them again. Both rows are parked until TR1 adds the count as a diagnostic.

items.title: The damage.spec mutant counts
items.body: The 17 and 33 differing frames are recorded in the commit message only. Ledger DR9 asks for a dev switch so they can be run again.

items.title: 0008:PR1: make the game's renderer and its first programs before the click
items.body: Aims at most of joining's ~850 ms first picture and the computer's ~925 ms.

items.title: 0008:TR1, then BR1 and SP1
items.body: Count triangles, parts and passes per frame as diagnostics (this also settles PS2 and BF1), then draw fewer triangles per pass for the move and the pick.

items.title: DR12 and EN1: the start page's bytes
items.body: Keep the damage code out of the preview's chunk, and the review's analysis out of the entry.

items.title: Checks: PX1, ZK1, DT1, DR9
items.body: Reset the backdrop's pass state on a lost context; pin the Zobrist keys; tighten two damage.test cases; let damage.spec see two partial frames in a row.
